item.title: Why Adding or Taking Away from God’s Word Is Spiritually Dangerous
item.description: From Eden to Revelation, God warns against altering His Word. Dave Jenkins explains why Scripture is final, sufficient, and authoritative, and why tampering with it leads to deception.

item.title: Job 4, Eliphaz Speaks and the Counsel of Assumption
item.description: In Job 4, Eliphaz responds to Job’s suffering with confident assumptions rather than compassionate wisdom. This episode explains why theology without humility wounds the weary and why Scripture must guide faithful counsel.

item.title: Centering Prayer Examined: Scripture, Silence, and Spiritual Deception
item.description: In this episode of Contending for the Word, Dave Jenkins examines centering prayer in light of Scripture, exposing the dangers of silence-centered spirituality and calling believers back to Christ and the sufficiency of God’s Word.

item.title: How to Cultivate Biblical Literacy at the Start of the Year
item.description: How to Cultivate Biblical Literacy at the Start of the Year By Dave Jenkins The start of a new year often brings renewed resolve. We reflect on where we’ve been, consider where we are, and think carefully about where we’re headed. Goals are set, habits are evaluated, and priorities are reshaped. item.title: How Christians Can Delight in God’s Word Daily, Even in Busy or Dry Seasons
item.description: How can Christians delight in God’s Word when life feels busy or spiritually dry? Dave Jenkins explains how simple faithfulness, prayer, and meditation renew joy in Scripture, even in dry seasons.

item.title: The Spiritual Dangers of New Age Healing and the Call to Biblical Discernment
item.description: A former New Age teacher and healer explains why practices such as Reiki and energy healing are spiritually dangerous and calls Christians to biblical discernment rooted in Scripture.

item.title: Job 5, Misapplied Discipline and the Danger of Weaponized Theology
item.description: Dave Jenkins walks through Job 5, explaining why not all suffering is God’s discipline and why Scripture must be applied with humility, compassion, and discernment.
